ra: Heaven is a principal realm of the structured Christian cosmos.
Hell is a principal realm of the structured Christian cosmos.
Purgatory is the intermediate purifying realm of the Christian cosmos.
The Limbo of the Fathers is a region of the Christian otherworld cosmos.
The Limbo of the Infants is a theorized region of the Christian cosmos.
The Empyrean is the highest heaven, the innermost dwelling of God within Heaven.
The New Jerusalem is the consummated heavenly city, the perfected form of Heaven.
Christian tradition identifies the Bosom of Abraham with the Limbo of the Fathers, the rest of the righteous dead before Christ.
The Beatific Vision is enjoyed by the blessed in the Empyrean, the highest heaven.
Dante's nine descending circles are the structural articulation of Hell.
Dante's seven terraces are the structural articulation of Mount Purgatory.
Dante's nine revolving celestial spheres are the ascending structure of Heaven below the Empyrean.
Dante places Limbo as the first of the nine circles of Hell.
Hell is the abode of the Devil; Dante fixes Satan at the center of the Inferno.
The demons inhabit Hell with their prince the Devil.
In the Harrowing of Hell, Christ descends and liberates the righteous held in the Limbo of the Fathers.
The Christian conception of Hell as the place of eternal punishment develops from the Jewish Gehenna.
The Bosom of Abraham as the rest of the righteous dead draws on the older Israelite Sheol as abode of the dead.
Augustine systematizes and transmits the heavenly Jerusalem as the City of God in De Civitate Dei.
